subject: Demo follow-up: proposed 6-week evaluation sprint & success map
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Reynolds <kate@northbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Demo follow-up: proposed 6-week evaluation sprint & success map

Kate — thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concise evaluation plan in writing so your team can review and confirm. The goal: validate a Redwood-hosted inference path that reliably extracts structured clinical intent and supports triage for your intake workflows while meeting latency and cost targets.

Attached: northbridge-eval-sprint-mup-v1.pdf (proposed mutual action plan), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

High-level proposal (6-week evaluation sprint)
- Objective: measure accuracy, latency, and end-end integration risk on a representative subset of Northbridge intake data.
- Success criteria (we recommend you confirm/adjust):
  - Extraction accuracy: >= 88% F1 on your labeled intent/entity set (primary bar)
  - Latency: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 900ms for typical 512 token requests when routed to hosted variant
  - Cost target: baseline operating cost < $0.007 per inference (token-based estimate) to be evaluated in Week 3
  - Integration: sample end-to-end run in your staging environment with synthetic or redacted data by Week 4
- Scope / deliverables:
  - Week 0 (this week): kickoff, data access plan, test dataset ingestion (sample: 2k records)
  - Week 1–2: baseline model runs, metric collection, and quick wins (prompt + routing tweaks)
  - Week 3–4: optimization (batching, quantization profile, cache prefixes), retraining if needed, privacy checklist
  - Week 5: validation on withheld dataset, SLA projections
  - Week 6: handoff and decision meeting (go/no-go & next steps for Dedicated or Private deployment)
- Owners & points-of-contact:
  - Northbridge: Kate Reynolds (project lead), Dev Ops Team (eng+northbridge@northbridgehealth.com)
  - Redwood: Marissa Cole — Customer Success (overall program owner), Ben Carter — Solutions Eng (technical lead), Irene Choi — Sales (exec sponsor)

Pre-kickoff asks from Northbridge (so we can accelerate):
- Provide a sample of 2,000 de-identified intake records (CSV or JSONL) + schema mapping
- Confirm whether evaluation must run in your VPC / on-prem or if pseudonymized hosted data is acceptable
- Primary procurement contact for minor PO/agreement items so we can share the mutual action plan

Next steps — please reply with the dataset ETA and procurement contact. I’ve attached a draft mutual action plan (MUP) that lays out timelines and responsibilities; if that looks directionally right we can lock a kickoff on the calendar. I’m available Tue/Thu mornings PT.

Thanks — I’ll stand by to update the plan based on your notes.

— Irene

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: proposed 6-week evaluation sprint & success map

Irene — thanks for the clear write-up and the MUP. A few clarifying items from our side before we schedule kickoff:

1) Compliance / hosting model: we need a SOC 2 summary and confirmation of whether the sprint can run entirely in our AWS account (VPC) rather than sending any PHI outside our environment. If hosted pseudonymized data is required, we need the exact pseudonymization steps documented.

2) Dataset format: we can provide CSV or JSONL; are there preferred column names you expect? Also confirm whether synthetic records are acceptable for weeks 0–2 while we prepare redacted real data.

3) Procurement: please send the MUP as a Word doc and any minimal SOW language so procurement can start review. Our PO team is cc’d.

If those items are covered, we are happy to lock in a kickoff on the 14th or 15th (mornings PT).

— Kate
Kate Reynolds
Head of Product, Northbridge Health
kate@northbridgehealth.com

Kate — quick technical notes and answers to your questions: great to meet you on the call.

- SOC2 / compliance: attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary + pointer to our auditor's report). For the sprint we can run entirely in your AWS account using Redwood Private connectors (we'll bring a lightweight runtime image into your VPC). That requires a short network allowlist and a temporary IAM role for ingestion. If you prefer hosted pseudonymized flows we will share step-by-step pseudonymization and mapping docs.

- Dataset expectations: JSONL with one record per line is preferred; include an id, free-text intake field, and optional labeled fields. Example manifest header: {id, intake_text, created_at, label_intent (optional)}. Synthetic data is fine to start — many customers use synthetic for early tuning and then swap in redacted samples for validation. Aim for at least 2k examples for baseline and 1k withheld for validation.

- Pre-kickoff checklist (attach in MUP):
  - PO/contract signoff (procurement contact)
  - Sample dataset (S3 path or secure upload)
  - Staging credentials / allowlist for VPC run if desired
  - Target metric set (confirm label schema for F1 calculation)

Proposed kickoff windows: Tue Sep 14 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed Sep 15 09:00–10:00 PT. I can lead the technical kickoff and walk through the ingestion/manifest steps.

Attaching: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attachment stub). Also added a short runbook to the shared drive: https://redwood.app/drive/nb/nap-1432 (link).

— Ben
